question: Who among the following participated in the All-World Religious Conference (Parliament of Religions) held in 1893 in Chicago?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Swami Vivekananda**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Swami Vivekananda represented India and Hinduism at the Parliament of the World's Religions held in Chicago in 1893.
 
• He is best known for his speech which began with the words "Sisters and brothers of America," which earned him a standing ovation from the audience.
 
• His speech at the Parliament is considered one of the most significant events in the history of modern Hinduism and Indian nationalism.
 
• Swami Vivekananda was a key figure in introducing the Indian philosophies of Vedanta and Yoga to the Western world.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **All-World Religious Conference (Parliament of Religions):**

 
 
• The Parliament of the World's Religions was an event held in 1893 in Chicago to create a global dialogue of faiths.
 
• It was the first organized interfaith gathering, bringing together religious leaders from various faiths around the world.
 
 
 
• **Swami Vivekananda:**
 
 
• Born as Narendranath Datta on 12 January 1863 in Kolkata, he was a chief disciple of the 19th-century Indian mystic Ramakrishna Paramahamsa.
 
• He played a major role in the revival of Hinduism in India and contributed to the concept of nationalism in colonial India.
 
• Vivekananda founded the Ramakrishna Math and the Ramakrishna Mission, which are still active in providing social services and spiritual teachings.
 
 
 
• **Hinduism and Vedanta:**
 
 
• Hinduism is one of the oldest religions in the world, encompassing a variety of philosophies, beliefs, and rituals.
 
• Vedanta is a school of Hindu philosophy that emphasizes the ideas found in the Upanishads, such as the ultimate unity of all existence and the essential oneness of the individual soul (Atman) with the supreme reality (Brahman).
